report:
Reviewed the complete parse.detail_firewall claim, four ordinary implementation entries, one ordinary test and one TODO test. Requirements: rebuilding a module can change syntax/absolute position without reminting unchanged semantic identity; represented definitions own separate syntax storage so equal siblings can backdate independently. Captured modules design and the linked identity/storage architectural rationale.

LocalFnSym separates stable name/scope/associated owner fields from tracked CST and tracked absolute span. LocalModSym similarly separates name/edition/parent identity from tracked body source, attributes and span; child membership is a separate tracked/specifiable query. parse_str_to_cst builds symbols via per-item parser dispatch. parse_fn allocates a fresh Stash, parses its declaration and body with item-relative coordinates, wraps the root in Stashed, and supplies absolute location separately. Other represented item constructors in items.rs likewise create independent stash-backed syntax products for structs/enums/traits/impls/types/consts/statics/invocations; modules and uses keep their own attribute/detail stashes, and macro definitions own attribute storage and body token text. Nested associated syntax initially belongs to its owner CST; captured associated-item lowering copies each minted member into its own stash, preserving the per-definition boundary at symbol creation. This is separate syntax ownership, not a promise that parsing never reads a containing source file again.

Captured util.rs establishes item-relative syntax spans and separately composed absolute spans. Captured Stashed ownership/fingerprinting shows equality is based on rooted content rather than the allocation identity of a newly rebuilt stash. Thus rebuilding equal per-item values can be backdated independently even when another item changes. Source inspection supports that representation; it does not establish the complete edit/invalidation matrix.

Ordinary test detail_edits_preserve_local_symbol_query_keys uses twelve cases: function body, struct field, enum payload, trait method declaration, impl method body, alias target, const/static value, module doc attribute, use target, macro definition output and macro invocation tokens. Each creates a persistent Database, observes the represented item, confirms warm observer reuse, changes SourceFile text via Setter, rebuilds and asserts that observe_symbol_identity does not execute again. The helper inside the annotated test rejects Error items before conversion. Captured setup_root_module actually parses the source and specifies membership; ObservedSymbol interns the Symbol and the tracked observer is keyed solely by that identity. Captured WillExecute logging and take_query_log explain why a newly minted identity would execute a new observer key. This is substantive identity stability evidence rather than a no-op assertion, though the observer intentionally does not read item detail.

The test does not directly assert changed CST contents, equal sibling fingerprints, moved source spans, insertion/reordering behavior or generated-item stability. The associated TODO modules_parse_detail_firewall explicitly reserves persistent moves/body edits/sibling insertion and reorder cases checking identity, CST fingerprints and downstream execution separately, including generated items. It has no assertions and is retained as deferred verification. Completing it needs multi-item persistent fixtures and independently observed identity/detail consumers so changed and unchanged products can be distinguished, plus generated source edits. The current single-item observer evidence is not represented as completing that matrix. No N/A evidence applies.

Commands executed: fresh cargo meta review start with coordinator instructions, exact source and complete-test inspection, review read captures for modules design/RFD, observer/root fixture, database execution logging, Stashed storage, associated-item copying and span helpers. An overlong util line-range read was rejected and replaced by a successful whole-file capture. No tests or build run by this reviewer; central execution remains separate evidence. No source changes or new suspected behavioral defect. No requested edits, retaining the explicit sibling/location/generated-item verification TODO.
